title: Locking the Tree of Space
src: Juspay hiring challenge (Unstop Part A / Hackathon A)
body:
The world is an m-ary tree of places, given in level order: node 0 is the root and the children of node i are nodes m·i + 1 … m·i + m. Users can lock places:

  • lock(X, uid) succeeds only if X is not locked and no ancestor and no descendant of X is locked. Then X is locked by uid.
  • unlock(X, uid) succeeds only if X is locked by the same uid. Then X is unlocked.
  • upgrade(X, uid) succeeds only if X is not locked, no ancestor of X is locked, X has at least one locked descendant, and every locked descendant is locked by uid. Then all those locks are released and X is locked by uid.

Print true or false for every query.

Function to complete

Complete lockTree(m, names, op, name, uid). It returns one boolean per operation: whether it succeeded.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: Line 1: n m q. Line 2: the n place names in level order. Next q lines: op name uid where op is 1 (lock), 2 (unlock) or 3 (upgrade).
cons: 1 ≤ n, q ≤ 5·10<sup>4</sup> in this mock (up to 5·10<sup>5</sup> in the real test)
1 ≤ uid ≤ 10<sup>9</sup>; names are unique and have no spaces

samples.in:
7 2 4
World Asia Africa China India SouthAfrica Egypt
1 China 9
1 India 9
2 India 9
2 Asia 9
samples.ex: China and India are siblings, so both locks work. Asia was never locked, so unlocking it fails.

samples.in:
7 2 5
World Asia Africa China India SouthAfrica Egypt
1 China 9
1 India 9
3 Asia 9
1 China 9
3 World 7
samples.ex: Upgrading Asia releases China and India and locks Asia. China now has a locked ancestor, and World's only locked descendant belongs to uid 9, not 7.
